events.title: The Teutonic Order defeats the Poles at the Battle of Płowce
events.description: At Płowce, forces of the Kingdom of Poland fought the Teutonic Order; the Poles were defeated, but their leaders escaped capture.
events.html: At Płowce, forces of the Kingdom of Poland fought the Teutonic Order; the Poles were defeated, but their leaders escaped capture.

events.title: The Treaty of Melno fixes the Prussian–Lithuanian border
events.description: Signed near Lake Melno by the Teutonic Knights and the Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, the treaty ended the Gollub War. The Order gave up its claims to Samogitia, and the border it fixed lasted about five centuries.
events.html: Signed near Lake Melno by the Teutonic Knights and the Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, the treaty ended the Gollub War. The Order gave up its claims to Samogitia, and the border it fixed lasted about five centuries.

events.title: Suleiman the Magnificent begins the siege of Vienna
events.description: Suleiman the Magnificent attacked Vienna with over 100,000 men in the first Ottoman attempt to take the Habsburg capital, defended by no more than 21,000 under Niklas Graf Salm. The city held out until the siege ended on 15 October.
events.html: Suleiman the Magnificent attacked Vienna with over 100,000 men in the first Ottoman attempt to take the Habsburg capital, defended by no more than 21,000 under Niklas Graf Salm. The city held out until the siege ended on 15 October.

events.title: Pope Paul III approves the Society of Jesus
events.description: The bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally established Ignatius of Loyola's Jesuits. The order became a leading force of the Catholic Reformation, founding schools and missions worldwide.
events.html: The bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally established Ignatius of Loyola's Jesuits. The order became a leading force of the Catholic Reformation, founding schools and missions worldwide.

events.title: Venice surrenders Candia to the Ottomans
events.description: The Venetians handed over Candia, modern Heraklion, ending a siege of more than 21 years, one of the longest in history. Crete passed to Ottoman rule.
events.html: The Venetians handed over Candia, modern Heraklion, ending a siege of more than 21 years, one of the longest in history. Crete passed to Ottoman rule.

events.title: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens
events.description: George Stephenson drove Locomotion No. 1, hauling coal wagons and hundreds of passengers, on the opening run. It was the world's first public railway to use steam locomotives.
events.html: George Stephenson drove Locomotion No. 1, hauling coal wagons and hundreds of passengers, on the opening run. It was the world's first public railway to use steam locomotives.

events.title: Germany, Italy and Japan sign the Tripartite Pact
events.description: The three powers signed a ten-year military alliance in Berlin, pledging mutual aid if attacked by a power not yet at war, aimed chiefly at the United States. It formalised the Axis.
events.html: The three powers signed a ten-year military alliance in Berlin, pledging mutual aid if attacked by a power not yet at war, aimed chiefly at the United States. It formalised the Axis.

events.title: The Warren Commission report is made public
events.description: The commission's report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald alone had killed President Kennedy. Its findings have been widely debated ever since.
events.html: The commission's report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald alone had killed President Kennedy. Its findings have been widely debated ever since.
